speaker: Doctor
text: I need to ask a few questions to narrow down the cause. Was the infant born at term, and did they pass any meconium within the first 48 hours of life?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-day-old male infant. The infant was born via a home birth without complications. The mother reports that the infant has had bilious vomiting and has not been able to pass meconium since birth. She also notes that the infant's abdomen appears distended.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did the mother notice any unusual characteristics of the amniotic fluid, such as it being thick, pasty, or cloudy? Also, has the infant passed any urine since birth?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Bilious vomiting. I also have Inability to pass meconium, Abdominal distension.

speaker: Doctor
text: I see, thank you for that information. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray. REQUEST TEST: Sweat_Cl_Test.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Abdominal_X-ray: Dilated loops of bowel with no gas in the rectum, suggestive of a distal obstruction. Sweat_Cl_Test: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal sweat chloride test effectively rules out cystic fibrosis, which is a common cause of meconium ileus. Given the distal obstruction and lack of meconium passage, I suspect Hirschsprung disease. REQUEST TEST: Rectal_Biopsy.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Rectal_Biopsy: Absence of ganglion cells in the submucosa and myenteric plexus, consistent with Hirschsprung’s disease.

speaker: Doctor
text: The biopsy results confirm the presence of Hirschsprung’s disease due to the absence of ganglion cells. DIAGNOSIS READY: Hirschsprung's disease
